walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 1: Personal Portfolio — a core area of GCSE Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 1: Personal Portfolio brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 1: Personal Portfolio.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique uses crossing lines for tone?

Cross-hatching
Smudging
Tracing
Lines
Dots
Circles
Squares

mcqs.q: What were Impressionist painters primarily trying to capture?
options: Their feelings or first impressions of a scene.
Realistic depictions of everyday life.
Photographic accuracy.
The fleeting effects of light and atmosphere at a particular moment.

mcqs.q: Why is preserving white in watercolour important?
options: You can simply paint white over other colours later.
Photographic accuracy.
Because white is the most expensive colour.
White comes from the paper showing through - there is no true white pigment in traditional watercolour.
Because white is the most expensive colour.
Realistic depictions of everyday life.
Random nonsense without intent.
The unconscious mind, dreams, and Freudian psychology.
